cues.en: So, this right here is a bipolar junction transistor which is a pretty common kind of transistor.
cues.zh: 这里这个就是双极结型晶体管，是一种很常见的晶体管。

cues.en: And, this particular one is an NPN
cues.zh: 而这一个具体是 NPN

cues.en: transistor.
cues.zh: 晶体管。

cues.en: And so, this transistor is made up of three layers of silicon
cues.zh: 所以，这个晶体管由三层硅构成

cues.en: like this.
cues.zh: 像这样。

cues.en: And maybe maybe you can guess what it means for it to be an NPN transistor. These two layers of silicon are n type,
cues.zh: 也许你能猜到它是 NPN 晶体管意味着什么。这两层硅是 N 型，

cues.en: and this layer here is p type, so NPN.
cues.zh: 而这一层是 P 型，所以就是 NPN。

cues.en: And, if you haven't watched my previous video where I go into quite a bit of detail about what these n type and p type silicon is, you should definitely go back and watch that. Otherwise, the rest of this isn't going to make a whole ton of sense.
cues.zh: 如果你还没看过我之前的视频，我在里面详细讲了 N 型和 P 型硅到底是什么，那你一定要回去看看。否则，后面的内容你很难完全听懂。

cues.en: And so, this is an NPN transistor. And they make PNP transistors as well, but we'll just talk about NPN for now. And so, this here is the circuit diagram for a transistor, and it's got the three leads coming off of it. There's an emitter, a base, and a collector. And, if you look at the actual physical transistor, there's three leads coming off and this is the emitter. The middle one is the base, and this is the collector. Although, that's not really standardized, but in this particular case, that's how it works.
cues.zh: 这是一个 NPN 晶体管。他们也会做 PNP 晶体管，但这里先只讲 NPN。这是晶体管的电路图，它有三根引线接出来。分别是发射极、基极和集电极。如果你看实际的晶体管，会有三根引线接出来，这一根是发射极。中间那根是基极，这一根是集电极。不过，这个并没有真正统一的标准，但在这个具体情况下，就是这样。

cues.en: And, what a transistor does is it is a current controlled switch. And so, what that means is that if we establish
cues.zh: 晶体管的作用是，它是一个电流控制的开关。所以，这意味着如果我们建立

cues.en: a
cues.zh: 一个

cues.en: small current from the base to the emitter in this direction,
cues.zh: 从基极到发射极、沿这个方向的微小电流，

cues.en: the transistor will switch on and it will allow a very large current to flow from the collector to the emitter.
cues.zh: 晶体管就会导通，并允许很大的电流从集电极流向发射极。

cues.en: And sometimes, can also use this as an amplifier because a small current is amplified into a large current flow here.
cues.zh: 有时也可以把它用作放大器，因为小电流在这里会被放大成大电流。

cues.en: And so, first off, there's actually something kind of confusing about the way this diagram is drawn with this arrow like this, which is that in a circuit diagram and a lot of times, a lot of engineers like to think about positive current flow, which is current flowing from positive to negative,
cues.zh: 首先，这张图这样画箭头其实有点让人困惑，因为在电路图里，很多工程师常常习惯按正电流来想，也就是电流从正极流向负极，

cues.en: when in reality, it's the electrons that flow from negative to positive.
cues.zh: 但实际上，是电子从负极流向正极。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter which convention we use because,
cues.zh: 我们用哪种约定其实并不重要，因为，

cues.en: you know, as long as there's current flowing in one direction to the other, the current will have the same effect.
cues.zh: 你知道，只要电流从一个方向流向另一个方向，产生的效果都是一样的。

cues.en: But when we start to actually look at what's going on inside the transistor, it's easier to think of this in terms of the direction the electrons are flowing, instead of the conventional direction.
cues.zh: 但当我们真正开始观察晶体管内部发生的情况时，用电子流动的方向来理解会更容易，而不是用常规电流方向。

cues.en: And so, really, what's going on in here, even though the arrow is pointing this way, and we think of current flowing that way, in reality, the electrons are flowing from the emitter to the base. And so, we'll just turn all of this around for
cues.zh: 所以，实际上这里发生的是：尽管箭头指向这个方向，我们也认为电流朝那边流动，但实际上，电子是从发射极流向基极。因此，我们干脆把这一切反过来，为了

cues.en: this discussion here.
cues.zh: 这里的讨论。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: to kind of restate what it is that the transistor does
cues.zh: 稍微重述一下晶体管的作用

cues.en: in terms of electron flow, is that
cues.zh: 从电子流动的角度来说，就是

cues.en: a small flow of electrons from the emitter to the base will turn the transistor on and allow a large flow of electrons from the emitter to the collector.
cues.zh: 少量电子从发射极流向基极，会使晶体管导通，并允许大量电子从发射极流向集电极。

cues.en: So, if we look at it in
cues.zh: 那么，如果我们从

cues.en: this scenario,
cues.zh: 这个场景来看，

cues.en: this piece of n type material might
cues.zh: 这块 N 型材料可能

cues.en: be the emitter.
cues.zh: 就是发射极。

cues.en: This middle p type is the base.
cues.zh: 中间这块 P 型材料是基极。

cues.en: And then, this n type material over here is the collector.
cues.zh: 然后，这边的这块 N 型材料是集电极。

cues.en: And so, what we're going to do with the transistor is that
cues.zh: 那么，我们要对晶体管做的是

cues.en: we're going to try to put a bunch of electrons in over on this side and we want to get them out over on this side. But, if the transistor is OFF, then we're not going to get that current flow.
cues.zh: 我们会试着从这一侧注入一堆电子，再让它们从另一侧出来。但如果晶体管处于截止状态，就不会有电流流过。

cues.en: And, in order to turn the transistor ON, what we want to do is get a small current flowing
cues.zh: 而要让晶体管导通，我们要做的是让一股小电流流动

cues.en: through the emitter and out the base like this. And once we get that
cues.zh: 让它像这样流过发射极并从基极流出。一旦我们让这股

cues.en: small current flowing, then the transistor will turn on. We'll have a large amount of current able to flow all the way through it.
cues.zh: 小电流流动起来，晶体管就会导通。大量电流就能一路流过它。

cues.en: So, let's redraw this so we can kind of get a closer look at what's really going on in here.
cues.zh: 我们重画一下，好更仔细地看看这里到底发生了什么。

cues.en: So, if we take a closer look at what's going on in here, we've got the emitter here, which is n type material. And so, we have these extra electrons that are in here that are free to move around. We've got the base, which is p type material. So, we have these holes that are in here that are free to move around.
cues.zh: 那么，如果更仔细地看看这里的情况，这里是发射极，是n型材料。所以这里有这些多余电子，可以自由移动。这里是基极，是p型材料。所以这里有这些空穴，可以自由移动。

cues.en: And then, the collector is also n type, so there's electrons that are free to move around.
cues.zh: 然后，集电极也是n型，所以有可以自由移动的电子。

cues.en: But at each of these p n junctions,
cues.zh: 但在每一个p-n结处，

cues.en: remember, we have this depletion region,
cues.zh: 记住，我们有这个耗尽区，

cues.en: which I've kind of exaggerated here. We have this depletion region because the electrons from the n type material are going to fill in some of the holes in the p type material and kind of neutralize each other. And so, there are no charge carriers in
cues.zh: 这里我画得有点夸张。我们有这个耗尽区，是因为n型材料中的电子会填补p型材料中的一些空穴，并彼此中和。所以，在

cues.en: these depletion regions in here.
cues.zh: 这里这些耗尽区里没有载流子。

cues.en: And so, what happens is, if we want to
cues.zh: 那么，发生的情况是，如果我们想

cues.en: try to get a current to flow through this thing, maybe we'll hook up...
cues.zh: 让电流流过这个东西，也许我们会接上……

cues.en: Let
cues.zh: 让

cues.en: me move up here. If we hook up a battery here,
cues.zh: 我往上移一下。如果在这里接上电池，

cues.en: just across
cues.zh: 就跨接

cues.en: the whole transistor from the emitter
cues.zh: 整个晶体管，从发射极

cues.en: to the collector, and so this is the negative terminal, this is the positive terminal, and we're going to be thinking about electron flow here.
cues.zh: 到集电极，所以这是负极端，这是正极端，我们这里要考虑的是电子流。

cues.en: The negative terminal of the battery is going to kind of inject some
cues.zh: 电池的负极端会注入一些

cues.en: electrons
cues.zh: 电子

cues.en: into here. You know, this is going to become a little bit more or a little bit negatively charged. So, there's going to be a few more electrons that enter this area. And some of them might even kind of creep into this depletion
cues.zh: 到这里。你看，这里的负电会稍微多一点。所以，会有更多电子进入这个区域。其中一些甚至可能慢慢渗入这个耗尽

cues.en: region a bit if we get enough electrons to come in here. But we don't have a current flow here. We're
cues.zh: 区一点——如果我们让足够多电子进来。但这里没有电流流动。我们

cues.en: not drawing
cues.zh: 没有抽取

cues.en: electrons out of the base and adding more holes here. So, we're not going to see that diode action here because we don't have a,
cues.zh: 从基极抽取电子，并在这里增加更多空穴。所以，我们在这里看不到那种二极管效应，因为我们还没有

cues.en: you know, that point six volt differential between the
cues.zh: 你知道，就是那个 0.6 伏的压差，在

cues.en: emitter and the base yet.
cues.zh: 发射极和基极之间，还没有出现。

cues.en: So, we might have some more electrons coming in here, but nothing crazy is going to happen here.
cues.zh: 所以，这里可能会有更多电子进来，但不会发生什么剧烈的变化。

cues.en: At the same time, some of the electrons that are in the collector are going to be attracted towards the positive terminal of battery. And so, we'll
cues.zh: 同时，集电极里的一些电子会被电池正极吸引过去。所以，我们就会

cues.en: lose some of these
cues.zh: 失去一些这样的

cues.en: electrons
cues.zh: 电子

cues.en: that are going to get kind of attracted to the battery.
cues.zh: 它们会被电池吸引过去。

cues.en: So, really nothing
cues.zh: 所以，其实没什么

cues.en: too exciting has happened here yet.
cues.zh: 特别令人兴奋的事发生。

cues.en: No current is flowing, that's for sure.
cues.zh: 肯定没有电流在流动。

cues.en: But now, what happens when we try to turn on the transistor? So, when we try to turn on the transistor, what we're going to do is we're going to try to apply a small current from the emitter to the base. And so, we might have
cues.zh: 但现在，当我们尝试开启晶体管时会发生什么？那么，当我们尝试开启晶体管时，我们要做的是尝试从发射极到基极施加一个小电流。于是，我们可能有

cues.en: a small battery down here that we connect to the across the emitter and the base.
cues.zh: 这里下方的一个小电池，把它跨接在发射极和基极之间。

cues.en: And so now, if we just look at the emitter and the base, it looks like we have a diode and we're
cues.zh: 所以现在，如果我们只看发射极和基极，看起来我们有一个二极管，而我们

cues.en: kind of
cues.zh: 有点

cues.en: trying to get current to flow through it in the forward direction, what we call forward biasing this diode.
cues.zh: 试图让电流沿正向流过它，也就是我们所说的给这个二极管正向偏置。

cues.en: And so, what's going to happen is the same thing that we saw when we looked at the diode in the previous video.
cues.zh: 接下来发生的情况，和我们在上一个视频里看二极管时看到的是一样的。

cues.en: Electrons are going to come into the emitter here.
cues.zh: 电子会从这里进入发射极。

cues.en: And, we're also going to draw electrons out of the base. And so, when we draw electrons out of the base, we're adding holes here to the base.
cues.zh: 同时，我们还会把电子从基极抽走。而当我们把电子从基极抽走时，就相当于在基极这里增加了空穴。

cues.en: And as long as we get about 0.6 or 0.7 volts
cues.zh: 只要我们能达到大约 0.6 或 0.7 伏

cues.en: of current flowing in this direction, so if this is greater than about 0.7
cues.zh: 让电流沿这个方向流动，也就是说，如果这个电压大于大约 0.7

cues.en: volts, I think, for most transistors,
cues.zh: 伏——我想对大多数晶体管来说是这样，

cues.en: then
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: we're going to start actually getting current flow.
cues.zh: 我们就会真正开始有电流流动了。

cues.en: And so, these electrons are going to get, you know, close enough here that this depletion
cues.zh: 于是，这些电子会靠得足够近——你知道——使这个耗尽

cues.en: region will
cues.zh: 区将会

cues.en: shrink to the point where we now have charge carriers
cues.zh: 收缩到我们现在有载流子的程度

cues.en: all the way through here, and so we can carry a charge all the way through.
cues.zh: 一路贯穿这里，于是我们就能让电荷一路通过。

cues.en: So, now, this is where things get really interesting. So, we've got a bunch of things going on here. So, first, we've got lots of electrons entering the emitter over here from
cues.zh: 所以，现在事情变得非常有意思了。这里有很多事情在同时发生。首先，有很多电子从这里进入发射极，来自

cues.en: this battery here. But also, we've got electrons entering from this battery here.
cues.zh: 这边的电池。但同时，也有电子从这边的电池进入。

cues.en: Second thing that's going on is the emitter part of the
cues.zh: 第二点是，……的发射极部分，也就是

cues.en: transistor,
cues.zh: 晶体管，

cues.en: the way they manufacture these is the emitter is really heavily doped.
cues.zh: 它们的制造方式是，发射极掺杂得非常重。

cues.en: So there's there's a relatively higher concentration of of those phosphorus atoms here. So there's there's a lot of those extra electrons that are free to move around anyway. So there's there's actually a lot of electrons in here just just to start with.
cues.zh: 所以这里那些磷原子的浓度相对更高。所以这里本来就有很多可以自由移动的多余电子。所以其实这里一开始就有很多电子。

cues.en: The way they manufacture the transistor.
cues.zh: 他们制造晶体管的方式。

cues.en: And so, all of this means that once this emitter to base current gets going, this current this way
cues.zh: 所以，这一切意味着，一旦从发射极到基极的电流启动，这个方向的电流

cues.en: gets going,
cues.zh: 开始流动，

cues.en: we've got a lot
cues.zh: 我们会有很多

cues.en: of electrons here that are just going to start wandering into this base, or I think the technical term is diffusing.
cues.zh: 这里的电子，它们会开始游荡进基极，或者按术语说，是扩散。

cues.en: So, we're going to have a lot of electrons that are going to start diffusing into this base.
cues.zh: 所以，会有很多电子开始扩散进这个基极。

cues.en: And some of them are going to fill in these holes.
cues.zh: 其中一些会填补这些空穴。

cues.en: And a few of them are gonna come out down here.
cues.zh: 还有少数会从下面这里出来。

cues.en: But, there's something really interesting, which is this base is really thin.
cues.zh: 但有个很有意思的点：这个基区非常薄。

cues.en: That's the key. If this base were really thick, then, you know, they would all just flow
cues.zh: 这就是关键。如果这个基区很厚，那你知道，它们就会全都直接流

cues.en: down this way. But because the base is really thin, they're kind of close to this area in here.
cues.zh: 向这边。但因为基区非常薄，它们就有点靠近这里这个区域。

cues.en: And if you remember, when we looked at the way the depletion region forms,
cues.zh: 如果你还记得，我们看耗尽区形成方式的时候，

cues.en: way the the depletion region forms is there were electrons that were over here that went over here to fill in holes. And so, this area, because the electrons have left,
cues.zh: 耗尽区形成的方式是，这边有电子跑到这边来填补空穴。所以这个区域，因为电子离开了，

cues.en: is positively charged.
cues.zh: 带正电。

cues.en: So, there's this positive charge that happens here because we've got
cues.zh: 所以这里会产生正电荷，因为我们有

cues.en: those phosphorus atoms that were here, you know, that used to have an extra electron and they still have an extra proton, but that extra electron has gone over here. So, there's this positive charge here and there's a negative charge here as well to kind of offset that and that's where the electrons went.
cues.zh: 那些原本在这里的磷原子，你知道，它们以前多一个电子，现在仍然多一个质子，但那个多余电子已经跑到这边了。所以这里有一个正电荷，这里也有一个负电荷，多少把它抵消掉，而电子就是跑到那里去了。

cues.en: But, we have all these electrons that are just diffusing into the base. So, lots of electrons are coming in kind of this way.
cues.zh: 但是，我们所有这些电子都在向基区扩散。所以，很多电子正从这边过来。

cues.en: And all these electrons that are bunched up, they're gonna just
cues.zh: 所有这些聚集在一起的电子，它们会

cues.en: attracted to this positive charge. And so, a lot of these electrons will actually just sort of,
cues.zh: 被这个正电荷吸引。于是，很多电子其实就会，差不多是，

cues.en: you know, scoot right through this depletion region
cues.zh: 你知道，直接穿过这个耗尽区

cues.en: and get attracted here. And then, of course, once they enter the collector,
cues.zh: 并被吸引到这里。然后当然，一旦它们进入集电极，

cues.en: you know, they're
cues.zh: 你知道，它们就

cues.en: free to wander around just because, you know, just the same way as any of these other electrons are free to wander around. And of course, there's this positive terminal of this battery that's going to attract electrons out here.
cues.zh: 可以自由地四处游荡，因为，你知道，就像这些其他电子一样，可以自由地四处游荡。当然，这个电池的正极会把电子吸引到这边来。

cues.en: And so, you get this action where, you know, you've got all these electrons bunched up over here that are being drawn into the base by this little current. And once those electrons end up in the base, there's this really strong positive charge that's really close because the base is thin. I mean, key here is that the base is really, really thin the way they manufacture it.
cues.zh: 于是，就出现了这样的过程：你懂的，所有这些电子都聚集在这边，被这股小电流拉进基极。而一旦这些电子进入基极，就会有一个很强的正电荷离得非常近，因为基极很薄。我的意思是，关键就在于制造时基极做得非常非常薄。

cues.en: And so, electrons get drawn to this positive charge.
cues.zh: 于是，电子会被这个正电荷吸引过去。

cues.en: You know, they're already kind of moving this way, they just get drawn right across. And then once they're in the collector, they're perfectly happy to wander around here and they continue
cues.zh: 你看，它们其实已经在往这边走了，只是被直接拉过去。一旦进入集电极，它们就很乐意在这儿转来转去，然后继续

cues.en: on.
cues.zh: 下去。

cues.en: And so, with a really thin base, most of the electrons are actually going to
cues.zh: 所以，基极非常薄时，大多数电子实际上会

cues.en: make that leap through this depletion region
cues.zh: 跃过这个耗尽区，

cues.en: and complete this circuit. And so, just this small amount of current going this way, just enough to kind of get rid of this depletion region in here,
cues.zh: 然后完成这个电路。所以，只要这么小的电流往这边走，就足以大致消除这里的耗尽区，

cues.en: combined with the fact that you've got lots of electrons coming in from here, lots of electrons coming in from here, and the emitter, the way they manufacture it, is heavily doped. There's already a lot of electrons in here.
cues.zh: 再加上这里有很多电子流入，这里也有很多电子流入，而且发射极在制造时是重掺杂的，这里本来就已经有很多电子了。

cues.en: You know, as soon as they, as soon as you close this depletion region and they
cues.zh: 你知道，一旦它们，一旦你闭合这个耗尽区，它们

cues.en: start moving into the, diffusing into this base,
cues.zh: 就开始进入、扩散到基极，

cues.en: you know, because it's so thin, because you've got this positive charge here, most of them, 99%
cues.zh: 你知道，因为它很薄，因为这里带正电荷，它们中的大多数，99%

cues.en: of these electrons actually, are going to get swept
cues.zh: 这些电子实际上会被扫

cues.en: into the collector
cues.zh: 进集电极

cues.en: and complete this circuit. So just a small current here results in a very large current going through the transistor.
cues.zh: 并完成这个电路。所以这里只需很小的电流，就能产生通过晶体管的大电流。

cues.en: And that's how the transistor works as a current controlled switch. So, this small current flow here
cues.zh: 晶体管就是这样作为电流控制开关工作的。那么，这里这股小电流

cues.en: turns on the transistor and allows a very large
